summary: Wrote rtl/baud_gen.v with parameter DIV_W=16 and ports clk, rst_n, baud_div and tick16, matching arch.yaml. The counter cnt_q is reset synchronously to 0. The limit is baud_div-1, or 0 when baud_div is 0, which gives the zero clamp of REQ-008. tick16 is high when cnt_q >= limit, and the counter then returns to 0, so the tick period is max(baud_div,1) clk cycles. If baud_div drops below the running count, the >= compare forces a tick and a reload on the next edge, so the counter cannot hang. I have not run verilator or yosys, so no check has been confirmed to pass; the runtime checks are still pending.
assumptions: A baud_div change that raises the limit just lengthens the current period. One that lowers it below the count gives an immediate tick and a reload.
Cell count of about 420 is taken from arch.yaml ppa_estimate, which is an estimate, not a synthesis result.
During reset, tick16 can still be high, because it depends on baud_div and the counter is held at 0. It is not a spec output, and the downstream uart_tx and uart_rx are in reset at that time.
I could not run tools in this task, so I make no new pass/fail claim beyond what the supplied report records.
No failure details from the earlier attempts were provided, so I treat them as having no documented failure to learn from.
No simulation, synthesis or power tools were run in this task; all effects are qualitative.
Parity enable is parity_mode[0]^parity_mode[1], so mode 3 behaves as none; odd mode is parity_mode[1].
RX start detection is a falling edge on rx_sync (previous sample 1, current 0), with the previous-sample register reset to 1.

TX holds tx high after accept until the first tick16, then drives the start bit for exactly 16 ticks. This costs up to one bit period of start latency and makes the stop bit exactly 16*baud_div cycles.
TX tx_ready equals (state==IDLE), a registered-state decode that is 1 after reset.
Technology is sky130A / sky130_fd_sc_hd at 50 MHz per spec; library ICG cell (sky130_fd_sc_hd__dlclkp) availability is assumed but not checked.
The RX parity expected value is ^data ^ odd; parity_err is 0 when parity is disabled.
The first tick after reset comes after max(baud_div,1) cycles, since the counter starts at 0 and ticks at count limit.
The knowledge entries kb-ck-002, kb-fc-002, kb-tk-001 and kb-ck-001 were consulted during the run, as stated in the task; I did not see their content.
The lint_report.json (sha256:4a503b3fe400) is the final RTL-stage lint result of this run.
The report file reports/low_power.md is produced from report_markdown; the runtime performs the write.
The start-bit glitch re-check is a single sample of rx_sync at the 8th tick (counter value 7).
The sync2 q output is the last stage; STAGES is fixed at 2 in uart_top
Typical use is a mostly idle UART at low baud rates, so tick16 is high only 1 in baud_div cycles; this is an assumption, not measured.
baud_gen parameter DIV_W is set to 16 on instantiation
baud_gen, uart_tx and uart_rx exist with exactly the arch.yaml port names
clk is the only clock and rst_n is synchronous active-low, per the coding standard
parity_mode is latched at accept in TX and at start detection in RX, so a mid-frame change cannot hang or corrupt the FSM (REQ-023); the frame content is undefined in that case.
rx_data updates only at frame completion; frame_err, parity_err and rx_valid are 0 in every other cycle.
sync2 STAGES must be >= 2; the generate-free shift implementation uses a vector of STAGES bits, and STAGES=1 would still elaborate but violate REQ-005, so the default is 2 and it is documented
tick16 is a combinational decode of registered state (cnt_q and baud_div); it is not registered. It is a one-cycle pulse as long as baud_div is stable.
tick16 is a one-cycle pulse from baud_gen, and baud_div=0 clamping (REQ-008/006) is done in baud_gen.
uart_top port widths are taken from spec interfaces: tx_data 8, baud_div 16, parity_mode 2, rx_data 8
open_issues: Any clock gating would need CDC/STA/CTS review (REQ-005 single clock) and a DFT consideration; this is not covered here.

Back-to-back TX (REQ-013) inserts a gap of 1 cycle of IDLE plus the wait for the next tick16, which is at most about 1 tick plus 1 cycle and well under 1 bit period. The stop bit itself is exactly 16 ticks.
Equivalence check or formal re-run would be needed after any change to confirm no function change.
Lint and yosys results are not yet known. I will fix any warnings after the runtime reports the tool output.
Lint and yosys results are pending.
Lint results unknown until the runtime runs verilator and yosys

No switching-activity data (VCD/SAIF) exists. Needed: a gate-level or RTL SAIF from loopback runs at baud_div 1, 27 and 65535 and in idle, with parity modes 0/1/2, plus idle-line and back-to-back traffic profiles, then a power analysis (e.g. OpenSTA/OpenROAD report_power) with the same netlist.
Per-attempt history (Ada, Ada-C, Ada-I) and timing/cost data were not supplied, so I cannot say what slowed the run down; a human or the runtime should supply this if a time analysis is wanted.

REQ-011 asks for tx_ready low for exactly one frame time after accept. Because the start bit waits for the next tick16 and accept can occur at any cycle, tx_ready low time is 10 or 11 bit periods plus up to one tick of alignment wait. Needs human or Vera decision on the tolerance.
REQ-024 (verification) is only traceable as a comment in the top; it is implemented by the verification agents, not by RTL
Simulation or testbench results for the RTL stage were not provided and are not covered here.
The combinational tick adds a 16-bit compare to the tick fan-out path. If timing at 50 MHz is tight, tick16 could be registered, at the cost of one cycle of latency.
The target use case (duty cycle, baud rates) is unknown; the answer to whether gating pays off depends on it. This should be decided by a human.
baud_gen change affects REQ-006/007/008/023 and needs RTL owner agreement and full regression re-run, including the baud_div edge values 0, 1, 65535 and mid-run changes.
uart_rx does not check rx_sync at start-up; if rx is low after reset, no frame starts because there is no falling edge, which is acceptable but untested.

messages.summary: The lint report shows Verilator lint and Yosys elaboration both PASS with 0 blocking issues, no waivers, and no structure or port findings. No failure is visible in the provided input, so I wrote no lessons. The retrospective is limited to what the report and the task metadata support. Previous attempts (Ada: 1, Ada-C: 1, Ada-I: 1) are noted, but I have no logs for them and did not infer what happened in them.

Recommendations only; no savings are quantified because no switching-activity data (VCD/SAIF) or power-tool output exists. Main findings: (1) baud_gen runs a 16-bit counter, a 16-bit >= comparator and a 16-bit incrementer every cycle, which is the largest toggling logic. Mitigation: replace the >= compare with an equality compare plus a separate reload-on-change guard, or hold the counter when idle. Risk is moderate because of REQ-023 and REQ-006. (2) The uart_rx and uart_tx counters and shift registers are enabled by tick16, so they are natural candidates for enable-based clock gating, but their small size (about 20 flops each) makes ICG overhead likely to exceed savings. Do not gate unless a power analysis shows otherwise. (3) Operand isolation: the tx parity XOR tree and the rx parity reduction are small; the gain is marginal. (4) The 16-bit baud_div input and tx_data are not registered, so activity on those input ports propagates into the baud_gen comparator and subtractor even when idle. Isolation is possible only if a functional-equivalent hold is acceptable, and it changes timing relationship to baud_div changes (REQ-023). Power domains/power-gating are not recommended: sky130 flow support is unconfirmed and the design is too small.

Wrote rtl/uart_tx.v (IDLE/START/DATA/PARITY/STOP) and rtl/uart_rx.v (IDLE/START/DATA/PARITY/STOP/WAIT_HIGH) to the arch.yaml ports, with REQ trace comments. TX aligns the start bit to the first tick16 after accept so every bit lasts exactly 16 ticks. RX counts ticks from falling-edge detection and takes the 3-sample majority at ticks 7, 8 and 9. No tool has been run on these files, so no check is claimed as passed.

Wrote sync2.v and uart_top.v. sync2 has a STAGES parameter (default 2), both flops reset to 1 synchronously. uart_top has the spec ports, instantiates baud_gen, uart_tx, uart_rx and sync2 with the port names from arch.yaml, and carries REQ-003/004/005/024 trace comments. No tools were run by me, so no pass is claimed; lint and yosys results are pending from the runtime.
